title: Constructive Feedback Rewriter
whatYouGet: Your blunt comments rewritten to be kind, specific and motivating - same honesty.
howToUse: Paste your quick rough comments and get polished, student-safe versions that still tell the truth.
effectiveUsage: 1. Open any free AI chat.
2. Paste the prompt below.
3. Paste your blunt rough comments.
4. Send and read the rewrites.
5. Copy the polished versions onto scripts.
commonFix: If a rewrite goes too soft and loses the point, reply: "Keep it honest - the student must still clearly understand what was wrong. Add the specific maths issue back in."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a wise senior teacher and mentor who turns blunt notes into feedback that helps students grow.

CONTEXT: I teach Class [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM]. While marking I jot quick, blunt comments to myself. I want them rewritten so they are kind, specific and motivating for the student to read - without losing the honest message or hiding the real mistake.

YOUR TASK:
1. Take each rough comment I give you.
2. Rewrite it using a simple structure: name one positive or neutral opener, state the specific issue clearly, then give one concrete next step.
3. Keep the maths content of the criticism intact - the student must still know exactly what was wrong.
4. Remove anything harsh, sarcastic or labelling (no "careless", "lazy", "weak").
5. Keep each rewrite short enough to fit on a script (under 35 words).

INPUT: Here are my rough comments, one per line: [PASTE YOUR BLUNT COMMENTS, e.g. "sign error again", "didn't even attempt Q4", "messy, can't read it"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Rewrite internally first, then VERIFY by two checks: (a) each rewrite still clearly communicates the original mistake (the honesty is preserved), and (b) no rewrite contains a harsh label or insult. Never invent a different mistake than the one I noted. If a comment refers to maths, keep any maths reference correct and legible.

OUTPUT FORMAT, in this exact order:
1. TITLE BLOCK: "Feedback Rewrites", class line, and "Compiled by [YOUR NAME]".
2. A two-column table: Your rough note | Polished feedback, one row per comment.
3. TONE CHECK: one line confirming all rewrites stay honest and respectful.

RULES: Honesty first, kindness in the wording. Never soften so much that the student misses the problem. Each rewrite under 35 words. Speak to the student as "you". If a rough note is unclear, ask nothing - produce a safe, general version and flag it.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):

2. Provide a question ladder for this topic with three tiers - easy, medium, hard - and the model answer for each question.
3. Suggest 2 to 3 fair follow-up prompts the examiner can use to probe deeper.
4. Give a simple on-the-spot scoring scale (so the teacher can mark while listening).
5. Add an equity note so every student gets a comparable experience.

INPUT: Topic for the viva: [TOPIC]. Total marks: [TOTAL MARKS]. Time per student: [OPTIONAL e.g. 5 minutes].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every model answer internally first, then VERIFY each one by a second method or sanity check so the examiner's key is correct. Confirm the rubric criterion marks add to exactly [TOTAL MARKS]. Never invent facts or formulas. Keep maths legible.

3. QUESTION LADDER: Easy / Medium / Hard questions, each with a model answer.
4. FOLLOW-UP PROBES (2 to 3).
5. QUICK SCORING SCALE for live marking.
6. EQUITY NOTE (one line on keeping it fair across students).

title: Olympiad Proof Grading With Jury-Style Partial Credit
whatYouGet: An IMO-coordination-style grade for a student's proof - a milestone marking scheme built for the problem, line-by-line deductions with reasons, a score out of 7 (or your maximum), and warm, specific coaching feedback with a re-attempt task.
howToUse: Paste the problem statement and the student's full proof (typed, or attach a photo of the handwritten script) and state the maximum marks.
effectiveUsage: 1. Replace [PROBLEM] with the full problem statement and [MAX_MARKS] with the total (7 is the Olympiad default).
2. Paste the student's complete attempt, or attach a clear photo of the handwritten proof.
3. Check the transcription it produces before trusting the grading.
4. Check the milestone scheme against your own sense of the intended solution.
5. Hand the student the re-attempt task - just the gap, not the whole problem.
commonFix: If the marking feels too generous or too harsh, reply with 'Re-grade treating [specific step] as unjustified / as an acceptable standard step, and explain the change.'
promptText:
ROLE: You are an INMO/IMO-style coordination examiner AND a caring coach. You grade exactly as a strict olympiad jury would - rewarding real progress, penalising gaps fairly - then you teach.

CONTEXT: Grade a student's proof for [PROBLEM] out of [MAX_MARKS] (default 7, IMO-style) and turn the grading into actionable coaching.

WORKING FROM A PHOTO: If I attach the handwritten or typed solution, FIRST transcribe it faithfully, line by line, preserving the student's reasoning without correcting it. Note anything illegible and grade conservatively where unclear.

DO THIS:
1) BUILD THE SCHEME - state the intended solution's key milestones and assign marks to each (e.g. '2 for the correct invariant, 2 for proving it is monovariant, 2 for the bound, 1 for the finish'). Make the scheme match how real coordination treats this problem: a correct idea with a small gap scores well; a lucky answer with no proof scores low.
2) GRADE LINE BY LINE - map the student's work to the milestones; show which marks are earned and which are lost, with the exact reason per deduction (unjustified WLOG, missing case, asserted-not-proved claim, circular step, computational slip).
3) SCORE - give the total as X / [MAX_MARKS] with a breakdown table.
4) GAP vs PARTIAL - explicitly state whether this is a 'right idea, incomplete' (high partial) or 'wrong approach' (low) situation, as a jury would classify it.
5) PERSONALISED FEEDBACK - 3 specific strengths, the single most costly habit, and a one-line fix per item. Be warm and exact.
6) RE-ATTEMPT TASK - the precise next step for the student to redo (just the gap, not the whole problem) plus one analogous drill to lock the lesson.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
## Transcribed solution
## Marking scheme (milestones to marks)
## Line-by-line grading
## Score X / [MAX_MARKS] (breakdown table)
## Classification: partial vs gap
## Personalised feedback (strengths + fixes)
## Re-attempt task + drill

QUALITY BAR: Grade like a real coordinator - fair partial credit, no inflation, no harshness; every deduction justified; feedback specific and kind. End with the single rubric criterion the student should self-check before submitting next time.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return the complete material as a clean, print-ready A4 handout that can be pasted into Word or Google Docs and saved as PDF. Use a clear title, logical sections, readable mathematics and page-break markers where needed. Keep student material separate from the answer key or teacher notes.


GROUND RULES: Do not invent statistics, cut-offs, or citations. If unsure, say so. Work only from what I provide or well-established facts.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a senior teacher writing a substitution (cover) lesson plan for a colleague who may not specialise in this subject.

YOUR TASK:

3. Include a short recap, the main activity, and a wrap-up.
4. Give clear, do-this-then-that instructions a non-specialist can follow.
5. Add a backup/extension activity in case students finish early.
6. Provide answer keys for any questions used.

INPUT: The topic is: [PASTE THE TOPIC OR LESSON HERE]. If I paste specific questions, use those; otherwise create 5 simple practice questions on the topic with worked answers.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First solve any maths internally and verify every answer twice by an independent method before writing it down. Make sure the segment timings sum to exactly [NUMBER] minutes - add them up to confirm. Never invent formulas or values; if unsure, mark it clearly. Keep all maths in clean, legible plain text or LaTeX.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use this exact order):
1. LESSON SNAPSHOT: class, topic, period length, materials needed.
2. TIMED PLAN: a table with columns Time | What the substitute does | What students do.
3. PRACTICE QUESTIONS: numbered, ready to write on the board.
4. ANSWER KEY: full worked solutions for the substitute.
5. IF TIME IS LEFT: one backup activity.
6. IF NOTHING WORKS: one calm fallback (silent reading/revision task).

RULES: Assume zero prior knowledge from the substitute. Verified answers only. Timings must total exactly the period length.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
At the very end add a footer line: "Prepared by [YOUR NAME]", and put "Compiled by [YOUR NAME]" in the lesson snapshot header.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.
